Subject: Atlas Bank — requests re: LLM data use & subprocessors

Hi Tessa and Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Atlas Bank Procurement and Legal are doing a quick evidence check before we move to an SOW. We have three concrete asks tied to our DPA review and regulator expectations:

1) Formal confirmation that Redwood will not use Atlas Bank customer data to improve or further train models (no-training/no-derivative use) unless we explicitly opt in.
2) A full, dated subprocessor inventory with locations and whether any processing occurs outside APAC (list roles and cloud providers).
3) Operational proof points for how prompt/response ownership is preserved (audit logs, exportability, redaction options, SFTP export).

If you can provide a packaged evidence bundle (redacted as needed) and a short technical mapping for our security team, we can keep the procurement timeline intact. Also looping in Jacob (outside counsel) on the legal Qs.

Appreciate a point estimate for delivery by end of week (Friday).

Best,
Olivia

Thanks Tessa — quick legal framing from our side:

- For procurement, an executed confirmation (signed addendum) that Atlas Bank data will be excluded from model training is sufficient in most cases; we should avoid language that creates unilateral model governance obligations (keeps scope narrow).
- Jacob: I’ll send the proposed addendum text separately if you want to review redlines.

Technical asks for Dev: can you assemble:
  * subprocessor-inventory.csv with columns: name, role, primary-region, processing-type (storage/compute/monitoring), last-updated
  * a one-page mapping showing where prompt/response logs live and the export path (API -> KV cache -> ephemeral logs -> optional SFTP)
  * note any subprocessors that have cross-border processing (specifically APAC -> US transfers)

PD: Atlas asked about audit logs and exportability — include a sample log snippet and retention policy.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

On so-called opt-outs: we usually support tenant-level flags to prevent model-learning; Ops/Eng provide the enforcement evidence.

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas Bank — requests re: LLM data use & subprocessors

Marissa/Tessa/Olivia — attaching the requested artifacts (zipped for transport). Quick technical summary here first:

Attachments included:
- redwood-no-train-evidence-v1.zip (contains: optout-flag-screenshot.png, audit-log-sample.txt, export-playbook.md)
- subprocessor-inventory.csv (detailed below)
- sftp-setup-instructions.pdf (runbook for scheduled exports)

Key points:
1) No-training enforcement
  - Tenant-level flag: tenant.config.model_learning = false. When set, inference requests are handled on a hardened path: log writes are tagged as "non-attributable" and excluded from downstream training ingest pipelines by filter rule ID RL-EXCLUDE-2027.
  - We store an immutable audit record of the flag being toggled (who/when) and daily snapshots of filter rules.
2) Prompt/response ownership & export
  - Prompt and response traces are retained under the customer namespace. Customers can request full export via API or scheduled SFTP. Audit-log sample shows the export job id and file checksums.
3) Subprocessor inventory (excerpt):
  - CloudCompute Ltd (compute) — primary-region: ap-southeast-1 — processing-type: compute — notes: model runtime; subprocesses are restricted by role-based ACLs.
  - ObjStore Inc (storage) — primary-region: ap-southeast-1 — processing-type: storage — notes: S3-compatible; encryption-at-rest with CMEK option.
  - TelemetryOps (monitoring) — primary-region: us-west-2 — processing-type: monitoring — notes: aggregated telemetry only; no access to tenant raw traces.
  - LoggingPartner (archival) — primary-region: eu-west-1 — processing-type: archival — notes: archival buckets for long-term logs; we can configure region restrictions per contract.

Cross-border notes: current default processing for Atlas tenant will keep compute and storage in APAC if requested; monitoring and aggregated telemetry are global by default but we can offer onshore telemetry ingestion for regulated workloads.

Operational runbook for evidence delivery:
- Step 1: Provide Atlas with redacted audit-log-sample and optout confirmation (attached).
- Step 2: Deliver subprocessor CSV and provide a point-of-contact for each vendor under NDA.
- Step 3: Coordinate SFTP export validation with Atlas security (we can run a test export into Atlas-managed S3).

I’m available for a call to walk Atlas Security through the artifacts Thursday 10am APAC / Wednesday 6pm PDT.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai

--
